subproblem.title: Cubical Stokes: the boundary of an integer polyhedral n-chain is an integer polyhedral (n−1)-chain
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, and β assign an integer to each pair. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfy T(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{(0,1)ⁿ} ω(Φ_p y)(e_ι) dy for all test n-forms ω. Then there are a finite set s' of index pairs q = (ι', b'), with ι' : Fin m → Fin P strictly increasing, and integers β'_q such that ∂T(γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q ∫_{(0,1)^m} γ(Φ_q y)(e_{ι'}) dy for every test m-form γ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 (boundary part) of the parent proof, “Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,1]ⁿ give [[F]](dγ) = Σ_j (−1)^{j−1}([[G_j^1]](γ) − [[G_j^0]](γ))”. Simon asserts this integrality without proof after (38) (chapter-06.txt lines 1922–1928); (37) is the corresponding mass bound. Here the indices j are 0-based, so the sign is (−1)^j.

Notation. n := m + 1; Q₁^k := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1}. For a pair p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P: Φ_p(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}, E_p := (e_{ι(j)})_j, and [[p]](γ) := ∫_{Q₁^k} γ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy. For y' ∈ Euclid m, j ∈ Fin n and a real c, insertNth j c y' ∈ Euclid n is the point with j-th coordinate c and remaining coordinates y' in order.

1. Faces of a face. For p = (ι, b) ∈ s, j ∈ Fin n and ε ∈ {0, 1} put q(p, j, ε) := (ι ∘ succAbove j, b + ε·𝟙_{ι(j)}), where 𝟙_{ι(j)} ∈ ℤ^P is the indicator of the coordinate ι(j). ι ∘ succAbove j : Fin m → Fin P is strictly increasing. Coordinatewise one checks Φ_{q(p,j,ε)}(y') = Φ_p(insertNth j ε y'): at ι(j) both sides equal b_{ι(j)} + ε; at ι(succAbove j l) both equal b + y'_l; elsewhere both equal b_i. Also E_{q(p,j,ε)} = E_p ∘ succAbove j.
2. dγ as a divergence. Fix p ∈ s and a test m-form γ. Define G : Euclid n → Euclid n by G(y)_i := (−1)^i γ(Φ_p y)(E_p ∘ succAbove i). G is C^∞. By SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply (removeNth i v = v ∘ succAbove i) and the chain rule (DΦ_p(y)e_i = e_{ι(i)}): dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[γ(·)(E_p∘succAbove i)](Φ_p y)(e_{ι(i)}) = Σ_i ∂_i G_i(y).
3. Divergence theorem on the unit cube. Let Ĝ(z) := ofLp(G(toLp z)) on Fin n → ℝ. Apply Mathlib's integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable' (with Mathlib's n := m) to f_i := (Ĝ ·)_i, a := 0, b := 1 and the empty exceptional set. Continuity, differentiability and integrability of the divergence hold because Ĝ is C^∞ and Icc 0 1 is compact. It gives
 ∫_{Icc 0 1} Σ_i ∂_i Ĝ_i = Σ_i (∫_{Icc 0 1} Ĝ_i(insertNth i 1 z') dz' − ∫_{Icc 0 1} Ĝ_i(insertNth i 0 z') dz').
 Transport these integrals to Euclid n and Euclid m with the measure-preserving maps ofLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp). The closed box Icc 0 1 and the open box Set.pi univ (Ioo 0 1) differ by a null set. So
 ∫_{Q₁^n} Σ_i ∂_i G_i(y) dy = Σ_i (∫_{Q₁^m} G_i(insertNth i 1 y') dy' − ∫_{Q₁^m} G_i(insertNth i 0 y') dy').
 (Equivalently: for each i, Fubini in the other m coordinates and the fundamental theorem of calculus in the i-th coordinate.)
4. Cubical Stokes. By steps 1–3, G_i(insertNth i ε y') = (−1)^i γ(Φ_{q(p,i,ε)} y')(E_{q(p,i,ε)}). Hence
 ∫_{Q₁^n} dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_{i∈Fin n} (−1)^i ([[q(p,i,1)]](γ) − [[q(p,i,0)]](γ)).
 For m = 0, Q₁^0 = Euclid 0 is a point of volume 1 and [[q]](γ) = γ(Φ_q 0)(()), the evaluation at the vertex.
5. Boundary of T. ∂T(γ) = T(dγ) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p Σ_{i∈Fin n} Σ_{ε∈{0,1}} (−1)^i (2ε − 1) [[q(p,i,ε)]](γ).
6. Regrouping. Let A := s × Fin n × {0,1} (a finite set), κ(p, i, ε) := q(p, i, ε) and c(p, i, ε) := β_p (−1)^i (2ε − 1) ∈ ℤ. Put s' := κ(A) (finite) and β'_q := Σ_{a∈A, κ(a) = q} c(a) ∈ ℤ for q ∈ s' (β'_q := 0 otherwise). Every q ∈ s' has strictly increasing first component (step 1). Grouping the finite sum of step 5 by the value of κ (Finset.sum_fiberwise / sum_image') gives Σ_{a∈A} c(a)[[κ a]](γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q [[q]](γ). Therefore ∂T(γ) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q ∫_{Q₁^m} γ(Φ_q y)(E_q) dy for every test m-form γ. ∎

dγ(Φ_p y)(e_ι) = div G(y) with G_i(y) = (−1)^i γ(Φ_p y)(e_ι∘succAbove i).
Divergence theorem on [0,1]ⁿ (integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable', transported by ofLp): [[p]](dγ) = Σ_j (−1)^j([[q(p,j,1)]](γ) − [[q(p,j,0)]](γ)).
Regroup the finite family (p, j, ε) by the resulting face to get integer coefficients β'.

subproblem.title: Geometry of unit lattice faces: unit-cube volume, isometric face maps, diameter, separation of distinct faces
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ: (0) the open unit cube Q₁^k = {y ∈ ℝ^k : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i} has Lebesgue measure 1. For all index pairs p = (ι, b), q = (ι', b') with ι, ι' : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing and b, b' ∈ ℤ^P, write Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (Euclid k → Euclid P). Then: (a) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y'. (b) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') ≤ √P for y, y' in the closed cube [0,1]^k. (c) If p ≠ q, y ∈ Q₁^k and y' ∈ [0,1]^k, then dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') ≥ 1, or there is j with dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1 ∧ ∀ p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → (∀ y y' : Euclid k, dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = dist y y') ∧ (∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ≤ Real.sqrt P) ∧ (p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma 2.1 and the face notation in step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, §5, chapter-06.txt lines 1841–1918, where faces F ∈ L_n and their interiors F̆ are used), written for faces of any common dimension k, as the parent proof notes.

Notation. Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^P. For an index pair p = (ι, b), with ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing and b : Fin P → ℤ, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Q₁^k := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i} and C^k := {y : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 ∀ i}. For v ∈ ℝ^P and every coordinate i, |v_i| ≤ ‖v‖ (‖v‖² = Σ_i v_i²).

1. Volume. ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and Q₁^k = ofLp⁻¹(Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1)), a measurable box. Hence vol(Q₁^k) = Π_{i : Fin k} vol(Ioo 0 1) = 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo). For k = 0 the empty product is 1.
2. Coordinates. Since ι is injective, Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j [ι(j) = i] y_j. This equals b_i + y_j if i = ι(j), and b_i if i ∉ range ι.
3. (a) Isometry. Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y') = Σ_j (y_j − y'_j) e_{ι(j)}. By step 2 its i-th coordinate is y_j − y'_j if i = ι(j) and 0 if i ∉ range ι, and each i is hit by at most one j. So ‖Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y')‖² = Σ_j (y_j − y'_j)² = ‖y − y'‖², i.e. dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y').
4. (b) Diameter. For y, y' ∈ C^k, |y_j − y'_j| ≤ 1 for all j, so dist(y, y')² ≤ k. Since ι : Fin k → Fin P is injective, k ≤ P. By (a), dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') ≤ √k ≤ √P.
5. (c) Set-up. Let p = (ι, b) ≠ q = (ι', b') (ι, ι' strictly increasing), y ∈ Q₁^k, y' ∈ C^k, x := Φ_p(y), z := Φ_q(y'). Then dist(x, z) ≥ |x_i − z_i| for every i.
6. Case A: some j has z_{ι(j)} ∉ (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)} + 1). Since x_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j with 0 < y_j < 1, every real outside that open interval is at distance ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) from x_{ι(j)}. Hence dist(x, z) ≥ |x_{ι(j)} − z_{ι(j)}| ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j): the second alternative holds.
7. Case B: b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1 for every j, so no z_{ι(j)} is an integer.
 (i) range ι ⊆ range ι': if ι(j) ∉ range ι', step 2 for q gives z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} ∈ ℤ, which is impossible. Both ranges have k elements, so they are equal. Two strictly increasing maps Fin k → Fin P with equal ranges coincide: each sends j to the (j+1)-st smallest element of the range (induction on j). So ι = ι'.
 (ii) b and b' agree on range ι. For each j, z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} + y'_j ∈ [b'_{ι(j)}, b'_{ι(j)} + 1] and z_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ, so b'_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋. Likewise b_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋.
 (iii) As p ≠ q and ι = ι', b ≠ b'. By (ii) there is i ∉ range ι with b_i ≠ b'_i. By step 2, x_i = b_i and z_i = b'_i are distinct integers, so dist(x, z) ≥ |b_i − b'_i| ≥ 1: the first alternative holds.
8. Cases A and B are exhaustive. For k = 0 there is no j, so Case B applies with empty ranges and gives dist(x, z) ≥ 1. This proves (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: vol(Q₁^k) = 1 via the measure-preserving ofLp onto the box Π(0,1).
Coordinates Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + y_j (i = ι(j)) or b_i (i ∉ range ι). Injectivity of ι makes Φ_p an isometry, so the diameter on [0,1]^k is ≤ √k ≤ √P.
Separation, case A: some coordinate z_{ι(j)} of the other point leaves (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)}+1), giving distance ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
Case B: otherwise range ι = range ι', so ι = ι', and b' agrees with b on range ι (floors). Then p ≠ q forces distinct integers b_i ≠ b'_i at some i ∉ range ι, giving distance ≥ 1.

subproblem.title: Currents given by integrable densities on finitely many faces: existence, mass, boundary mass and support (Simon (29)–(30), (34))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Then some compact K contains every tsupport ω_j, and (taking the iterated derivative of order 0, whose norm is ‖ω_j(x)‖) ω_j → 0 uniformly on K. By the chain rule, with DΦ_p(y)e_i = e_{ι(i)}, ∂_i (G_p)_i(y) = (−1)^i D[γ(·)(E_p∘succAbove i)](Φ_p y)(e_{ι(i)}). Assume also that Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q). Then either ξ(α) = α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α.

Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Simon (26), chapter-06.txt lines 1841–1847: on the interior of a face lying in ℝⁿ × {0}, the current is a current of the plane oriented by ±e₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ eₙ), isolated as a statement about approximate tangent planes (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and unit orientations.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1; e := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}); V := {v ∈ ℝ^P : v_i = 0 ∀ i ∉ range ι}. Since ι is injective, V is a closed subspace, V = span(range e), and e is an orthonormal basis of V, so finrank V = n.

1. Blow-ups lie in V. For r > 0 and a ∈ A, blowUpMap x r a = r⁻¹(a − x), and (a − x)_i = 0 for i ∉ range ι by hypothesis. So S_r := blowUpMap x r '' A ⊆ V.
2. Q ⊆ V. Suppose q ∈ Q ∖ V. V is closed, so d := infDist(q, V) > 0. Let f(y) := max(0, d/2 − ‖y − q‖). f is continuous, f ≥ 0, f > 0 on ball(q, d/2), and f = 0 outside closedBall(q, d/2), so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Also f = 0 on V, since ‖v − q‖ ≥ d for v ∈ V.
 (i) For r > 0, the open set O := {f ≠ 0} is disjoint from V ⊇ S_r. So (Hⁿ⌞S_r)(O) = Hⁿ(O ∩ S_r) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply, O measurable). Hence f = 0 Hⁿ⌞S_r-a.e. and ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ = 0. (S_r need not be measurable; only O is measured.)
 (ii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q says ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺. The left side is 0 for all r > 0, and 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter, so ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.
 (iii) The same hypothesis gives finrank Q = n. So the support of Hⁿ⌞Q is Q (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, SimonGMT Ch. 3), and ball(q, d/2) has positive Hⁿ⌞Q-measure because q ∈ Q. Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compacts (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), so the bounded, compactly supported, continuous f is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable. Since f ≥ 0 and {f > 0} ⊇ ball(q, d/2) has positive measure, ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). This contradicts (ii). Hence Q ⊆ V.

subproblem.title: The (n−1)-skeleton of the unit lattice is Hⁿ-null
subproblem.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ, the set L_m := {x ∈ ℝ^P : there is s ⊆ {0,…,P−1} with P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} (points with at least P − m integer coordinates) satisfies μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0.

1. Countable cover. For s ⊆ Fin P and z ∈ ℤ^P put A(s, z) := {x : x_i = z_i ∀ i ∈ s}. If x ∈ L_m with witness s, then x ∈ A(s, z) for z_i := x_i (i ∈ s) and z_i := 0 otherwise. 3. dimH(A(s, z)) = dimH(ψ '' univ) ≤ dimH(univ : Set (Euclid r)) (LipschitzWith.dimH_image_le) = r (dimH_univ_eq_finrank). Since r ≤ m < m + 1 = n, hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt gives μH[n](A(s, z)) = 0.

proof_key_steps: Cover L_m by the countably many coordinate affine planes A(s, z) = {x_i = z_i (i ∈ s)} with P ≤ m + |s|, z ∈ ℤ^P.
Each A(s, z) is the range of an isometry from Euclid r with r = P − |s| ≤ m. Hence dimH A(s, z) ≤ r < m + 1, so μH[m+1](A(s, z)) = 0 (hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt).
Countable subadditivity and μHE[m+1] = c·μH[m+1] give μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0.

Following the parent proof, the variation on a face is bounded by V_p := M_{N_p}(∂Q₀) for explicit pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods N_p. The proof uses the hypothesis (VO) and the sibling face_geometry.

Notation. n := m + 1; Q₁, Cⁿ, Φ_p, E_p, F_p := Φ_p(Cⁿ), F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁) as usual (Φ_p(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}). For p = (ι, b) let p̃_p : ℝ^P → Euclid n, p̃_p(x)_j := x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)}. It is continuous and affine, with p̃_p(Φ_p y) = y and p̃_p(x + t e_{ι(i)}) = p̃_p(x) + t e_i. Let δ_p(t) := min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)) for t ∈ Euclid n. δ_p is continuous and positive on Q₁. Recall |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. For a degree-m current S on ℝ^P and an open W, M_W(S) = sup{ofReal(S γ) : tsupport γ ⊆ W, |γ(x)| ≤ 1 ∀ x}.

1. Neighbourhoods. N_p := {x : p̃_p(x) ∈ Q₁ and dist(x, Φ_p(p̃_p x)) < δ_p(p̃_p x)/2}. N_p is open (the open preimage of Q₁ intersected with a strict inequality of continuous functions). F̆_p ⊆ N_p: for x = Φ_p(y) with y ∈ Q₁, p̃_p x = y and the distance is 0.

The separation part of face_geometry (p ≠ q, t ∈ Q₁, y' ∈ Cⁿ) gives dist(Φ_p t, x) ≥ 1 or ≥ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for some j; either way dist(Φ_p t, x) ≥ δ_p(t). This contradicts dist(x, Φ_p t) < δ_p(t)/2.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 (first part) of the parent proof (parent E7(e); Simon Ch. 6, 5.1, after (38), chapter-06.txt lines 1922–1928: “the fact that P, R are integer multiplicity … should be evident”, and (36): M(P) = Σ|β_F|). Written for faces of any dimension k ≥ 0 so that it also applies to the boundary chains of the sibling chain_boundary. Uses the hypothesis (MR) and the sibling face_geometry.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k]; Q₁ := Q₁^k; Cᵏ := [0,1]^k. For p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing:
 - Φ_p, E_p := (e_{ι(j)})_j, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), F_p := Φ_p(Cᵏ);
 - Π_p := {x : x_i = b_i ∀ i ∉ range ι} = Φ_p(Euclid k);
 - V_p := span{e_{ι(j)}} = {v : v_i = 0 ∀ i ∉ range ι}, so Π_p − x = V_p for x ∈ Π_p;
 - e_p is the k-vector α ↦ α(E_p), and δ_p(t) := min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)) (= 1 for k = 0).

1. Facts from face_geometry. Φ_p is an isometry and vol(Q₁) = 1. For distinct p, q ∈ s and t ∈ Q₁, every z ∈ F_q has dist(Φ_p t, z) ≥ δ_p(t) > 0 (separation, with y' := Φ_q⁻¹(z) ∈ Cᵏ). In particular the F̆_p (p ∈ s) are pairwise disjoint. Each F̆_p = {x ∈ Π_p : b_{ι(j)} < x_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1} is Borel.
2. Change of variables (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Φ_p a measurable embedding). ∫_{F̆_p} h dHᵏ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy for Borel h ≥ 0 or h integrable on F̆_p. In particular Hᵏ(F̆_p) = vol(Q₁) = 1.
3. The triple. Let s⁺ := {p ∈ s : β_p ≠ 0} and C := ⋃_{p∈s⁺} F̆_p. Define θ(x) := Σ_{p∈s⁺} |β_p| 1_{F̆_p}(x) ∈ ℕ (Int.natAbs) and ξ(x) := Σ_{p∈s⁺} sign(β_p) 1_{F̆_p}(x) e_p. By disjointness, for x ∈ F̆_p with p ∈ s⁺, θ(x) = |β_p| ≥ 1 and ξ(x) = sign(β_p) e_p. The IMRep fields hold:
 - C is Borel and C ⊆ ℝ^P = U.
 - C is countably k-rectifiable: C ⊆ ⋃_{p∈s⁺} range Φ_p, each Φ_p is Lipschitz (an isometry), and finitely many maps can be listed as F_j, padded with constant maps (exceptional set M₀ := ∅).
 - θ is measurable, θ ≥ 1 on C, and ∫_{C∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ Σ_{p∈s⁺} |β_p| Hᵏ(F̆_p) < ∞ for every compact K.
 - ξ is measurable (finite sum of Borel indicators times constants), hence AE-strongly measurable.
4. Orientation and tangent plane at every x ∈ C. Let x ∈ F̆_p, p ∈ s⁺, x = Φ_p(t), t ∈ Q₁, and δ := δ_p(t) > 0.
 (i) IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) V_p: τ := E_p is orthonormal (ι injective), span(range τ) = V_p, and ξ(x)(α) = sign(β_p) α(τ) for all α.
 (ii) C ∩ B(x, δ) = Π_p ∩ B(x, δ). “⊆”: a point of C ∩ B(x, δ) lies in F̆_q ⊆ F_q for some q ∈ s⁺; q ≠ p is impossible by step 1; so it lies in F̆_p ⊆ Π_p. “⊇”: if z ∈ Π_p with |z − x| < δ, then z = Φ_p(t') with t'_j := z_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)}. By the isometry, |t' − t| = |z − x| < δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j), so 0 < t'_j < 1 and z ∈ F̆_p ⊆ C.
 (iii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x V_p. finrank V_p = k. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport f ⊆ B(0, R), and let 0 < r < δ/R. Then blowUpMap x r '' C ∩ B(0, R) = V_p ∩ B(0, R). Indeed, if z ∈ C and |r⁻¹(z − x)| < R, then |z − x| < δ, so z ∈ Π_p by (ii) and r⁻¹(z − x) ∈ V_p. Conversely, if v ∈ V_p and |v| < R, then z := x + r v ∈ Π_p with |z − x| < δ, so z ∈ C by (ii) and v = r⁻¹(z − x). The set blowUpMap x r '' C is Borel (the image of C under an affine homeomorphism), and f = 0 off B(0, R). So f·1_{blowUpMap x r '' C} = f·1_{V_p} pointwise, and ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' C} f dHᵏ = ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ for all 0 < r < δ/R. The limit as r → 0⁺ is therefore ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ. (For k = 0: V_p = {0}, Π_p = {b}, δ = 1, and the same computation holds with H⁰ the counting measure.)
 Hence R := (C, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P; its orients condition holds at every point of C.
5. R represents T. For a test k-form ω, ∫_C θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈s⁺} ∫_{F̆_p} |β_p| sign(β_p) ω(x)(E_p) dHᵏ(x) (a disjoint finite union; the integrand is bounded and C has finite measure). By step 2 this is Σ_{p∈s⁺} β_p ∫_{Q₁} ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy. Adding the vanishing terms with β_p = 0 gives T(ω). So T is integer multiplicity.
6. Mass. (MR) with U = W = ℝ^P (open) gives M(T) = M_{ℝ^P}(T) = R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈s⁺} |β_p| Hᵏ(F̆_p) = Σ_{p∈s} |β_p|, i.e. M(T) = ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} |β_p|).
7. Dichotomy. If β_p = 0 for all p ∈ s, then T(ω) = 0 for all ω, so T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Otherwise some |β_p| ≥ 1, as β_p is a nonzero integer, and M(T) = ofReal(Σ|β_q|) ≥ 1.
8. If k > P there is no strictly increasing ι : Fin k → Fin P, so s = ∅, C = ∅, and T = 0 with M(T) = 0; the steps above remain valid. ∎

IMRep: carrier ⋃_{β_p≠0} Φ_p((0,1)^k), multiplicity |β_p|, orientation sign(β_p)e_ι. It is rectifiable as a finite union of isometric images.

Near x in an open face the carrier equals the plane Π_p on B(x, δ_p), so the blow-ups agree with V_p = span e_ι on B(0, R) for small r. Hence V_p is the approximate tangent space and sign(β_p)e_ι orients it.

Simon gets Q⌞F̆ = θ_F[[F̆]] from the constancy-theorem argument 2.34–2.35. M is Borel. θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable, θ ≥ 1 on M, and ∫_{M∩K'} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K'. ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M. Let μ := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M.

4. L_n ∖ L_m is covered by open faces. Let x ∈ L_n ∖ L_m and J := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}. From x ∈ L_n there is s ⊆ J with P ≤ n + |s| ≤ n + |J|. From x ∉ L_m (test s := J), P > m + |J|, i.e. P ≥ n + |J|. Thus |g| ≤ C_ω θ 1_{tsupport ω} a.e. on M, which has finite integral, so g is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable. By step 7, ∫_M g dHⁿ = ∫_{⋃_{p∈s}(M∩F̆_p)} g dHⁿ. 13. Steps 5, 10, 11 and 12 give every conclusion. s is finite with ι strictly increasing. Each F_p meets spt Q₀. Each u_p is integer-valued everywhere and integrable on Q₁. The mass bound and the representation hold. ∎
